input.title: Construction's efficiency barrier is unstructured data even more than siloed data

input.description: Beyond fragmentation across CDE/Planner/Mural, the data itself is unstructured — risk management lives in disconnected Excel. Priorities: tasks, docs/metadata with access control, BIM-to-field.

input.content:
Agli Hysi's diagnosis of construction-project inefficiency has two layers, and the deeper one is not the one usually cited (DT BAU, 01:44:33):

1. **Data silos** — information fragmented across the CDE, Microsoft Planner, Mural, SharePoint and more, with no unified project overview (01:34:18).
2. **Unstructured data** — the data itself is not machine-readable. Risk management is the canonical example: risks are measurable (site plans, delivery schedules) but managed via disconnected Excel tables, so they never reach higher project-management levels in structured form (01:47:05–01:48:44).

Asked to prioritize three types of structured data for a future system (01:54:25):
1. **Tasks**
2. **Documents and model metadata** — with strict access control
3. **"BIM-to-field" data** — connecting construction-site progress to the digital environment

Cost management shows the same pattern: non-semantic Excel tables from stakeholders get manually transformed into dashboards (00:34:07). Structure-first document models attack the root cause where dashboard tooling only treats the symptom. A dependency graph over structured project data would enable proactive bottleneck monitoring (01:51:40).
